title: differential-approval-reconciliation-prd-wip
content:
Overview:
This is an early PRD for a feature we are tentatively calling 'Differential Approval Reconciliation' (DAR). The goal is to provide a compact, customer-friendly mechanism that reconciles approval gate decisions and customer-managed network events with Redwood's immutable audit stream, while minimizing bandwidth and storage for on-prem/VPC customers who opt into lightweight proofs rather than full log export.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Private deployments often need to prove to internal auditors that operator approvals, customer firewall handshakes, and control-plane decisions match the evidence kept by the customer. Full log replication is heavy and exposes lots of telemetry.
- Current approaches either ship raw audit streams (expensive, privacy concerns) or periodic summaries (coarse, hard to reconcile for short-lived failures).
- Customers ask for a way to: prove a decision happened, prove the decision parameters, and quickly reconcile mismatches at small cost in bytes/compute.

Key idea (in one sentence):
Produce small differential attestations (delta-proofs) that encode the changes to approval state and network handshakes over a reconciliation window, plus a compact Merkle-style proof that ties them back to the canonical audit ledger retained by Redwood.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Provide proofs small enough to be exported via low-bandwidth channels (S3/secure-email/SCION-like pipelines) and stored alongside customer evidence packs.
- Allow auditors to deterministically verify a sequence of approvals and network state changes for a specified time window without needing full logs.
- Support automatic reconciliation workflows (customer tool compares local evidence to Redwood proofs and flags deltas).
- Integrate with existing approval gate UX (canary/cancel/override) and with our immutable audit index.

Non-goals:
- This is not a replacement for high-fidelity SIEM export when customers require streaming audits in real-time.
- Not intended to provide deep packet or raw network telemetry — only metadata about approval and handshake events (who, what, where, why, artifact-hash).

User stories / personas:
- Platform Security Lead (enterprise): wants a tamper-evident receipt for each operator approval and the ability to reconcile within minutes if a rollback happens.
- Customer Network Admin (customer-managed VPC): wants proof that our edge orchestration executed the agreed handshake and that their firewall rules were applied.
- Internal Forensics Engineer (Redwood SRE): wants a compact ingestable artifact that can be attached to incident tickets to speed root-cause.

Core features / components (sketch):
1) Delta Attestation Blob (DAB):
   - A compact JSON-ish artifact (we'll spec binary-friendly encoding) containing: list of changes in time-order, per-change metadata (actor, approval-id, decision, policy-version, target-tenant, change-hash), and a short, incremental state-digest.
   - Each DAB is bounded by size (configurable, default 256KB) and covers a reconciliation window (configurable default 15m).
2) Canonical Audit Anchor (CAA):
   - For each DAB we emit an anchor that references the canonical audit ledger entry range and includes a Merkle root over the full set of raw events for that window (kept server-side).
   - Anchor includes signed timestamp, Redwood key-fingerprint, and a compact nonce to avoid replay.
3) Differential Proof Chain (DPC):
   - Chaining DABs over time via incremental digest so offline consumers can stitch reconstruction across windows even if some DABs are missing; missing windows are detectable.
4) Reconciliation API + CLI:
   - Endpoint for customers to submit DABs and request a verification result.
   - Local CLI that ingests the customer's local evidence pack (files, local logs) and the Redwood DAB+CAA to produce a human-readable reconciliation report and suggested action (match, drift, missing-events).
5) Policy-aware drift detection:
   - Reconciliation should classify differences by severity (benign metadata drift, policy mismatch, evidence missing, tampering suspicion).

Design notes / data shape (working):
- DAB (fields): sequence_start_ts, sequence_end_ts, window_id, entries[]. Each entry: event_type, operator, approval_id, decision, policy_hash, target_resource, change_hash, minimal_context_tags, request_ref (optional).
- CAA: anchor_id, window_id, merkle_root, server_range_ids, signed_at, signature, redwood_key_id.
- We will define a canonical canonicalization function for 'entry' before hashing to ensure stable change_hashes.

Security and trust model:
- Redwood signs CAA and DAB digests with a rotation-aware signing key (KMS-backed).
- Customers may optionally sign their local evidence bundle; reconciliation verifies dual-signed chains.
- Replay mitigation: window nonce + signed timestamp + sequence number.
- Privacy: DAB includes only minimal context tags; raw logs remain on Redwood unless customer enables full replication.

Operational considerations:
- Storage: store CAAs in cold ledgers with index for quick fetch. Keep raw events for configurable retention (customer contract dependent).
- Ingest: reconciliation endpoint validates signatures, verifies merkle_root against Redwood internal ledger, and returns a delta report.
- Scaling: DAB generation piggybacks on existing audit log writer; generation cost per window estimated at low CPU + sha256 ops.

Telemetry & metrics to track rollout:
- DAB generation rate (per-tenant), average DAB size, verification latency, % of reconciliations that report 'match' vs 'drift', false-positive rate (post human review), number of replays detected, storage delta vs full export.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- DAB + CAA produced for 15m windows for all Private deployments behind a feature flag.
- Signed CAA verifiable by internal test harness using Redwood public key.
- CLI checks a synthetic local evidence bundle and reports exact match for a seeded test case.
- Reconciliation endpoint returns a structured delta report and classifies severity.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Alpha (internal): implement DAB generation for one internal customer-simulated tenant, CLI used by SRE, follow up with manual audits. (2 sprints)
- Beta (selected customers): opt-in for 3–5 private deploy customers, expose DAB artifacts via S3/secure upload, iterate on report UX and classification. (4–6 sprints)
- GA: enable by contract, add billing + retention config + audit logs in Console. (3 sprints)

Open questions / risks (raw list):
- How small can DABs get while still giving actionable evidence? Need experiments with 5/15/60m windows.
- Merkle root construction: do we include full raw event payloads on the server side or only canonicalized metadata? Payloads increase auditability but raise privacy and retention cost.
- Compatibility with existing approval gate models (canary/override): ensure overrides produce a clear provenance chain in the DAB.
- Legal/Compliance: will customers view DAB as sufficient evidence for audits in regulated industries? We need legal review and sample auditor acceptance tests.
- Key management: customer-managed HSMs? If a customer requires Redwood to use customer-provided signing keys, add flow.
- Failure modes: what if a Redwood internal index entry is pruned before customer requests reconciliation? Need retention policy and TTL warnings.

Implementation sketch (engineering notes):
- Add a DAB writer component in the audit pipeline; write DABs to per-tenant storage and emit CAA signed objects.
- Expose a reconcile/verify endpoint behind private-deploy API gateway with strict auth.
- CLI: python3 tool that fetches DAB+CAA, ingests local evidence, canonicalizes local entries, verifies signatures, computes diff, outputs markdown report.
- Tests: unit canonicalization + property tests for incremental digest; integration harness that replays production-like event patterns.

Monitoring and support playbooks:
- When reconciliation detects 'tampering suspicion', auto-create SRE ticket with attached artifacts, and notify customer via secure channel asking for next-step (manual review, expunge, escalate).
- Provide a 'reconciliation audit' in Console UI that shows time-series of match-rate.

Notes / TODOs (short):
- [ ] Run size experiment with anonymized production events to calibrate default window and size cap. (Assignee: Marco)
- [ ] Draft canonicalization proto and publish for review. (Assignee: Ben)
- [ ] Legal review on 'proof sufficiency' for financial/healthcare customers. (Assignee: Sofia)
- [ ] Create CLI prototype and internal verification tests. (Assignee: Yuki)

References / inspirations:
- Compact attestation patterns (paper notes), Merkle-anchored proofs in supply-chain logs, small-bundle for disconnected forensic workflows.
- Related Redwood artifacts: CONFLUENCE-UI-1234 (approval UX sketch), JIRA-PDP-712 (private deploy audit retention epic).

This doc is intentionally rough — looking for feedback on the core tradeoffs (privacy vs. fidelity vs. bandwidth) and prioritization of the MVP acceptance criteria.

Appendix (example synthetic DAB - conceptual):
---BEGIN DAB---
window_id: rdw-20241115-1545
entries:
  - id: ap-000123
    event_type: operator-approval
    operator: alice@example.com
    approval_id: ap-000123
    decision: approved
    policy_hash: sha256:abcd...
    target_resource: tenant-42/route-7
    change_hash: sha256:ef01...
  - id: net-000321
    event_type: handshake
    operator: edge-orch@redwood
    decision: completed
    policy_hash: sha256:4321...
    target_resource: tenant-42/edge-conn-5
    change_hash: sha256:dead...
digest: sha256:feed...
anchor_ref: caa-rdw-20241115-1545
---END DAB---

(Real encoding will be binary-friendly and sized; above is illustrative.)
